It’s the penultimate challenge of the competition and the three remaining bakeries have their eyes on the prize.

Three bakeries from Greater Manchester and Cheshire vie for a place in Friday’s regional final.  An artisan baker goes up against traditional pasty purveyors, and a pair of chemists turned cake makers.

Judges Mich Turner MBE and Peter Sidwell continue their search for baking brilliance north of the border. Three independent Scottish Bakeries are out to impress them, but only one can stay in the competition.

Like many, Christmas is Mary Berry’s favourite time of year. But all that cooking and preparation comes with a lot of pressure. No matter how many times you’ve cooked for it before, it can all seem a bit daunting.

Tonight Mary takes inspiration from a great British tradition, growing your own on the allotment. Mary’s father turned his flowerbeds over to growing veg for the war effort and ever since then, Mary has been hooked on growing her own fruit and veg.

Mary cooks dishes inspired by her home and family. No matter how busy Mary is, her top priority is to have the family round for a meal, and tonight, three generations of Mary’s family visit her in the kitchen and get involved with the cooking.
One of Mary’s pleasures is to shop for fresh, exciting, seasonal ingredients, and tonight; it’s the local farmers' market that inspires Mary.
Enrobed in chocolate icing, this chocolate, butter, rum, and almond Reine de Saba is just the best chocolate cake you will ever eat.

st: Ham Dinner In Half An Hour
d: There comes a time when you have no time, yet it’s company time.  That’s the time for this chic three-course meal.
Lest we forget broccoli and cauliflower, Julia Child takes a fresh look at this talented twosome of the cabbage family.
Julia Child entertains at a formal dinner, starting with Coquilles Saint-Jacques a la Creole -- scallops in a buttery white wine sauce with truffles and fleurons served on a silver salver.

A French poached egg is not for breakfast.  It makes its appearance later in the day; it goes into a souffle, it is served with Bearnaise Sauce and mushrooms in a buttery tartelette, or it comes shimmering to the table cloaked in aspic.
Julia Child makes Daube and Carbonade de Beouf -- a classic Mediterranean duo. Each stew is easy to make, and each stew offers something new.
Judges Mich Turner and Peter Sidwell take their search to the South West of England, where three Devon-based bakeries enter the baking arena.
It’s the first day of Finals Week and just five bakeries are left in the competition to find Britain’s Best.

Older daughter, Megan helps with a mouth-watering crispy duck and her favourite dipping sauce. Gordon's Mum assists with a braised oxtail, followed by chilli poached pears, and Jack returns to help with his favourite dish, sticky spicy chicken wings.

The chef prepares cinnamon eggy bread with stewed apples. Youngest daughter Tilly helps with a hearty beef and ale stew, a sausage hotpot and a warming pear and ginger galette. Gordon’s Mum helps with Shepherd’s pie and a steamed date pudding.
